answer: A key is born when a garden signs it, and every key's saffron lock doubles with each live key under the same garden-tree — the lagoon, which holds all locks, burns a garden's whole stake and kills its line if any key under it is proven fake. A fresh root is itself a signed key, so it steps the same doubling; the only way out is paying an unrelated garden to adopt a clone outside the tree, a bribe that must cover that garden's entire forfeitable stake each time. To match one honest newcomer, who signs under an untouched garden at base saffron, the k-th clone freezes base × 2^k saffron.
